scenario: AITA for wanting my girlfriend to be less braggy about her work perks? She seems to forget that the way she lives isn't how most people live... | My girlfriend has a pretty sweet job. She doesn't have set hours; she just has to work 35 hours a week whenever is convenient for her and make it to her few meetings. She can work from the office or from home sometimes. She has a full benefits package despite being under what most people consider full time. A really nice retirement package too. And the company will pay everything for continued education. She does work she finds interesting (cutting edge robotics) and gets along well with her coworkers. She has a lot of PTO per year and her boss even lets the employees "earn up" more; if they work extra hours one week they can ask for the equivalent in PTO for later. Her team's managers buy them whatever they want for the office; they want a 500 dollar expresso maker, they get it. They want a type of fancy coffee, they get it. Nice furniture, done... They get paid well too; pretty middle of the road salary for robotics but she says the work life balance more than makes up for it. She'd rather have more time than be a top earner. And honestly a midrange robotics salary is still damn good. And anyway, For a while I thought "good for her" for having found something that she is happy with. But recently it's gotten frustrating because I think she forgets that this isn't how everyone lives. Like when we're out with my friends or just hanging out she'll talk about the nice stuff her managers bought for the office, about all the vacations she takes, about how she and her coworkers left the office in the middle of the day to see a movie then came back and just worked a little later. And yeah, it seems like she forgets that is no way a normal job. So last night we were at a party and she mentioned how she was going to tour a few new apartments Monday morning and afternoon, and one of the people at the party was like "don't you have work" and she said "yeah but I can set my own hours" And that just rubbed me the wrong way and I said that she needed to stop going on and on about her work perks, it was obnoxious and came off braggy. She was like "I was just explaining something" and I said it wasn't just this, it was everything. Most people don't live the life she lives." She said that I was coming off jealous and that it was a bad look. That she was where she was because she didn't settle for less; she studied and worked her ass off, and didn't let herself get too settled anywhere she was unfulfilled. And that instead of complaining, maybe I should ask myself what I'm feeling jealous of and what I need to do to get it. I told her she was missing the point; she'll always be around people who don't have what she does, and she could be a little more modest about it. She said I was the only one who seemed to have a problem with it, and stormed off... AITA for what I said?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the person in this scenario is AITA (Ask if I'm the Asshole) for wanting their girlfriend to be less braggy about her work perks. Let me break this down step by step. First, the girlfriend has a really great job with a lot of perks. She has flexible hours, can work from home, has a nice benefits package, good retirement plan, paid education, and a lot of PTO. She also gets to work on interesting projects and has a good work-life balance. It sounds like she's really happy with her job, which is awesome for her. But the issue is that the person feels she's bragging about these perks, especially when they're around friends or at parties. They mention that she talks about the nice office stuff, her vacations, and how she can set her own hours. The person feels that she forgets that not everyone has such a great job and that her behavior comes off as obnoxious or braggy. In the specific incident, at a party, she mentioned she was going to tour apartments during the day, and someone asked if she had work. She replied that she could set her own hours, which annoyed the person. They told her to stop going on about her work perks, and she got defensive, saying she was just explaining and that the person was jealous. So, is the person AITA for saying this? Let's consider both sides. On one hand, the person is feeling frustrated because they think their girlfriend is flaunting her job perks in a way that makes others feel inferior. They're pointing out that not everyone has such a great job, and they want her to be more modest. It's possible that the person feels left out or jealous, especially if they're in a different situation where they don't have such flexibility or benefits. On the other hand, the girlfriend feels that she's just sharing her positive experiences and that she worked hard to get where she is. She's proud of her achievements and doesn't see anything wrong with talking about them. She might feel that the person is being unnecessarily critical or jealous, which is why she got defensive. I think it's important to consider the context of their relationship. If the person has expressed these feelings before, maybe the girlfriend hasn't taken them seriously, leading to frustration. It's also possible that the person is projecting their own insecurities onto the girlfriend, which could be why they're reacting so strongly. However, the girlfriend's response of saying the person is jealous and should work on themselves might not be the best approach. It could make the person feel invalidated, which might escalate the situation. Instead, she could acknowledge the person's feelings and perhaps adjust how she talks about her job in social settings. In terms of whether the person is AITA, I think it's a bit of both. The person has a valid point that the girlfriend's behavior might come off as bragging, especially in social situations where others might feel less fortunate. But the way they addressed it could have been handled more gently. Instead of outright telling her to stop, they could have expressed their feelings in a more constructive way, perhaps suggesting that she's aware of how her comments might affect others. The girlfriend, on the other hand, should be more considerate of how her words might impact those around her, especially in mixed company. She doesn't have to hide her achievements, but being more mindful of the audience could help prevent others from feeling uncomfortable. So, in conclusion, while the person's frustration is understandable, the way they expressed it could be seen as a bit harsh. The girlfriend's reaction also doesn't help the situation. Both parties could work on communication to better understand each other's perspectives.
